content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 1
(as on 10.02.2025) Key Insights

1. Summer Sowing Status: Summer sowing data collection has been started from 7th February, 2025 and the sowing is in preliminary stage. 2. Rabi Season Area Coverage: o As of January 31, 2025, the total area sown under Rabi crops is 661.03 lakh ha, an increase from 651.42 lakh ha last year. Wheat sowing has reached 324.38 lakh ha, surpassing both last year’s 318.33 lakh ha and the normal 312.35 lakh ha. o For Rabi horticulture crops, major producing states report the following sowing areas: Onion – 9.67 lakh ha (8.40 lakh ha last year), Potato – 19.81 lakh ha (19.50 lakh ha last year), Tomato – 2.18 lakh ha (2.39 lakh ha last year). 3. Weather Update: a) Temperature: Minimum temperatures are likely to fall 2-3°C over Northwest, central & East India during next 3 days and no significant change thereafter. Maximum temperatures are likely above normal by 2-3℃ over south peninsular India during next 4-5 days and no significant change in minimum and maximum temperatures likely over rest parts of the country during next 5 days. Overall, rainfall is likely to be below normal over all the homogeneous regions of the country during the week. b) Rainfall Distribution: From January 01– February 09, 2025, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 71% below its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: -53%; (ii) Northwest India: -76%; (iii) Central India: -97%; and South Peninsula:-24% o Isolated to scattered light rainfall/snowfall activity likely over Arunachal Pradesh during 10th-15th increasing to fairly widespread to widespread rainfall accompanied with thunderstorm & lightning during 11th-13th February with isolated heavy rainfall on 11th & 12th February. o Isolated to scattered light rainfall/snowfall activity likely over Sub-Himalayan West Bengal & Sikkim during 10th-14th; northeast Assam during 10th-14th; Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram & Tripura during 10th-12th February. 4. Inputs Situation a) Water Reservoir Status: As of February 06, 2025, the live storage in 155 major reservoirs is 110.204 BCM (61% of total capacity). Storage is at 123% of last year’s level and 119 % of the 10-year average. The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period. b) Groundwater Levels: Approximately 66.6% of monitoring wells show water levels between 0-5 m, while 29.1% report levels between 5-10 m. Decadal analysis (2014–2023) indicates a rise in 64.9% of wells and a decline in 35.1% as of August 2024. c) Seeds and Fertilizers: For Rabi 2024-25, certified seed availability is 337.98 lakh quintals against a requirement of 307.07 lakh quintals, ensuring a surplus of 30.90 lakh quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products. 5. Pests & Diseases: Pest and disease intensity remains below Economic Threshold Levels (ETL), except for Chilli (Black Thrips: Thrips parvispinus) in Andhra Pradesh, where advisories have been issued, and monitoring is ongoing.

content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 3
Details of each Segment

1. RAINFALL During the week (30th Jan 2025 –05 Feb 2025), large deficient rainfall was observed, as compared to Long Period Average (LPA) by 59%. Cumulative seasonal rainfall (01 Jan to 09 Feb 2025) is lower than LPA by 71%.

Rainfall Forecast: 06th Feb – 12th Feb 2025 a) Isolated to scattered light rainfall/snowfall activity likely over Western Himalayan Region during 08th-12thFebruary, 2025. b) Isolated to scattered light rainfall/snowfall activity likely over Sub-Himalayan West Bengal & Sikkim during 10th-14th; northeast Assam during 10th-14th; Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram & Tripura during 10th-12th February. c) Overall rainfall is expected to be below normal across India during the week. 13th Feb – 19th Feb, 2025 a) No active western disturbance is likely to influence northwest India during the week. However, due to feeble Western disturbances, light/moderate isolated to scattered rainfall/snowfall likely over Western Himalayan Region during some/many days of the week. b) Light/moderate isolated to scattered rainfall is also likely over northeast India during some days of the week. c) Overall, rainfall is likely to be below normal over all the homogeneous regions of the country during the week.

content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 4
2. TEMPERATURE: MIN & MAX

Temperature Forecast 06th Feb – 12th Feb 2025 a) Minimum temperatures in Central India are expected to gradually drop by 2-3°C in the first half of the week, with no significant change afterward. b) In East India, a decline of 3-5°C is likely over the next two days, followed by stable conditions. c) Maharashtra will see no major temperature change in the next 24 hours, but a gradual rise of 2- 3°C is expected later in the week. Maximum temperatures will remain 3-5°C above normal across North Peninsular and East India for most of the week. 13th Feb – 19th Feb , 2025: d) Minimum temperatures are likely to be between 8-12°C over most parts of plains of northwest India, central & east India during the week. e) Minimum temperatures are likely to be below normal by 2-4°C over most parts of east and adjoining central & north Peninsular India during the week.

content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 6
4. REMOTE SENSING BASED SOIL MOISTURE OBSERVATION

Soil Moisture Observation  Soil moisture during 31 Jan- 06 Feb 2025 is better/similar to the average of the past 9 years in A.P, Karnataka, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Rajasthan, M.P, Punjab, Haryana, Western UP and Maharashtra.  Whereas lower than average of past 9 years avg. in Northern parts of Bihar, Northern W.B. and in parts of Chhattisgarh & Odisha.
5. CROP SOWING STATUS FOR RABI SEASON Preliminary area coverage of Summer Crops

 Rice: About 8.708 lakh ha area coverage under Summer Rice has been reported as compared to 8.044 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.  Pulses: About 0.299 lakh ha area coverage has been reported compared to 0.283 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.  Oilseeds: About 0.200 lakh ha area coverage has been reported compared to 0.177 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.

states and upto 09.02.2025, a quantity of 430.90 LMT of paddy in terms of Rice has been procured against previous season’s corresponding procurement of 419.17LMT.  Wheat: Procurement period in Rabi Marketing Season (RMS) 2024-25 is over in all procuring states and a quantity of 266.05 LMT of wheat has been procured whereas procurement in the previous marketing season (RMS 2023-24) was 261.97 LMT.  Actual stock of Rice & Wheat together was 489.74 LMT against buffer norm of 307.70 LMT.
